verdicts.reasoning: READ: stagedArtifact keeps only canPreviewArtifact kinds, which are site, report and spreadsheet (work-site-preview.tsx:164-166). WorkDeliverableStage is the only deliverable UI mounted in chat (rg finds its one importer at work-run-panel.tsx:14/357). WorkDocuments/DocumentCard have no importer (rg over src and tests). /work/* now just redirects to the chat (src/app/(app)/work/[[...segments]]/page.tsx:37-58). No other client code calls /api/work/artifacts. SessionOutputs builds tiles only from chat Artifacts and assistant IMAGE attachments (session-outputs.tsx:98-107,137-147). So the text '{n} more files under Outputs.' (stage:76) points at a popover that never holds Work files. One correction: the runner cannot make a PDF. create_deliverable accepts five spec kinds (tools.ts:966-978: document, report, spreadsheet, presentation, site), so the kinds that disappear today are .docx and .pptx, not PDF. The header comment (stage:25-29) still describes the retired rail's Outputs section, which is where the stale copy comes from.

READ: deleteAccountPermanently collects keys only from prisma.attachment plus their thumbnails and the avatar (delete-account.ts:43-53), then deletes the user (72). The runner writes `work-artifacts/<userId>/...` (work-runner.ts:1988). The route writes `uploads/<userId>/...` through buildObjectKey (route.ts:311; storage.ts:49-51). Cloud files go to `work/<userId>/<sessionId>/<name>` (work-runner.ts:1474-1476,1916-1921). WorkArtifact and WorkArtifactVersion cascade (schema.prisma:2628-2631,2660), so the rows go and the keys are lost. rg for deleteObject across src and scripts finds no caller that touches these prefixes, and no sweeper exists. One small overstatement: the DeletionReport counts attachments only and never claims Work objects were purged. The erasure gap itself is real.

READ: UNSAFE_MARKUP (validate.ts:643-654) runs over the whole text of every .html and .css entry (696-700), including escaped body text. VERIFIED with my own scratch probe through generateDeliverable. 'Set the flag one = true…' gives an inline-event-handler problem, 'Read javascript: the good parts.' gives a javascript: URL, 'We fetch (and cache)…' and 'Call fetch() to load it' give a browser network call, and '@import' gives a CSS @import. Each returns ok=false. 'Plain text only.' passes. A code block showing `fetch(url)`, which any JS docs site would contain, trips the same rule. The runner then sets validatedAt null and tells the model to say the file is unconfirmed (work-runner.ts:2021,2063,2083-2085).

READ: the list refetches only when load (sessionId), produced (artifacts.length) or enabled (run !== null) change (work-documents.tsx:100-103; use-conversation-work.ts:244). deriveArtifacts keys a Map by artifactId, so artifact_updated replaces the row and the count stays the same (work-detail-panels.tsx:181-201). agent-core emits artifact_updated for a known id (runner/agent-core/src/work/session.ts:580-588), and the runner reuses the DB artifact id across versions (work-runner.ts:2087-2094). Nothing calls reload (rg). The stage previews `version={artifact.currentVersion}` from the stale row (stage:68-73), but Download has no version param (stage:58), and the download route serves currentVersion (download/route.ts:64). So preview and download can disagree until the page reloads. This is reachable because the tool description invites re-publishing under the same identifier (tools.ts:1012).

READ: WorkDeliverableStage never reads validatedAt (stage:41-80). The download route only adds X-Juno-Validated and X-Juno-Validation-Warning headers (download/route.ts:156-157), which a plain anchor navigation never shows. The inline site and report previews render unvalidated bytes too. VerdictLine and the 'not confirmed to open' copy live only in the unmounted DocumentCard (work-documents.tsx:281). Combined with defect 3, ordinary sites are presented as fine.

READ: discovery asks fetchWorkSessions({conversationId, limit: 1}) and adopts the newest (use-conversation-work.ts:179-186; delegation.ts:99-106). ChatView adds one WorkRunPanel (chat-view.tsx:2267), while research also maps history (2263). A second task in one conversation is reachable: start_task is idempotent per user message, not per conversation (task-tool.ts:190-203), and chatTaskToolEnabled has no 'conversation already has a task' condition (157-174). Automation rows link /work/<sessionId>, which redirects to the conversation and so shows only the newest task. rg found no other web surface that lists a session's artifacts.

READ: the runner parses `{ spec: request.spec }` only (work-runner.ts:1826), and the tool's deps and inputSchema carry just identifier and spec (tools.ts:949-952,1015-1029). So generated.provenance is always [] and provenanceForStorage([]) is stored (2043). sourcesMarkdown and sourcesHtml return nothing for empty provenance (report.ts:337-351). Citations go only to source_cited events (work-runner.ts:1821). The route accepts provenance, but no client POSTs to it. Nuance: the model can still hand-write a 'Sources' heading in its blocks, but the structured, reviewable provenance is always empty.

READ: the limits are 20 bullets of 500 chars, 10 paragraphs of 2,000 chars, and table 20 rows x 10 cols x 300 chars (presentation.ts:30-39). Bullets and body go into a fixed 9x3.6in box at 16pt with no fit or shrink (177-192). addTable has no h and no autoPage (194-206). VERIFIED by probe: a 20-row table writes 21 `<a:tr h="0">` rows at y offset 1280160 EMU (1.4in), with cell marT and marB of 45720 EMU (0.05in). At 12pt that is at least about 0.3in per row, about 6.3in against the 4.2in left on a 5.625in slide. The row heights are inferred geometry, but the conclusion holds even with one-line cells. The validator counts slides only.

READ: the replay path compares head.contentHash (route.ts:287-305). The test file itself says the OOXML kinds embed a timestamp (tests/work-deliverables.test.ts:268-270), and spreadsheet.ts sets workbook.created = new Date(). VERIFIED by probe: xlsx, docx and pptx hashes differ between two generations about 1.1s apart, while report hashes match. The problem is latent. Native only GETs (NativeWorkClient.swift:433-474), no web code POSTs, and the runner has its own write path with no replay check.
READ: document.ts:243-253 skips the title when blocks[0] is an H1 but always pushes the subtitle first. VERIFIED by probe: the w:t order is ['Sub','Body H1','p'].

READ: paragraphs use escapeMarkdownLineStart (report.ts:172), but list items (175-177) and quotes (181) use inlineMarkdown only. MARKDOWN_INLINE does not escape '#', '-' or digits followed by '.'. VERIFIED by probe: the output is '- 3. Third step
- - dash lead
- # not a heading

> # quoted hash', while a paragraph correctly becomes '\# para hash'. Under CommonMark these parse as nested lists or headings.

READ: `z.object({ date: z.string().datetime() })` (spreadsheet.ts:66), while the tool guide says '<ISO 8601>' (tools.ts:972). VERIFIED by probe: '2026-03-04' fails with 'Invalid ISO datetime'. It is worse than claimed: '2026-03-04T00:00:00+01:00' is also rejected, because only the Z form is accepted.
READ: NUMBER_FORMATS.currency = '"$"#,##0.00' (spreadsheet.ts:85), and spreadsheetColumnSchema has no currency or locale field (90-95).

READ: cellText returns String(value) for numbers and never reads numFmt (spreadsheet-preview.ts:79-96). The preview shape carries no format either. VERIFIED by probe: the rows are ["1234.5","0.256","1234567"] for the currency, percent and integer columns. This contradicts the header's 'nothing lost that a reviewer was going to check' (5-13).

READ: WorkDeliverablePreview returns WorkReportPreview for report and WorkSitePreview for every other previewable kind (work-site-preview.tsx:353-357). No dialog exists for spreadsheets (the only spreadsheet shell is the inline one at 388-393). DocumentCard shows Preview and mounts WorkDeliverablePreview for any canPreviewArtifact kind (work-documents.tsx:284-293,419-428). Latent only, because WorkDocuments has no importer.

READ: putObject runs at work-runner.ts:1989-1994. The deleted-identifier and kind-conflict checks throw inside the later transaction (1996-2007) with no deleteObject. The route does these checks before its putObject (route.ts:257-285), so the runner is the path that leaks. rg for sweep, orphan and ListObjects finds only the import-run sweeper, and nothing covers the work-artifacts/ or work/ prefixes. Other upload routes do clean up (upload/route.ts:135).

READ: the route enforces IDENTIFIER and a max of 120 (route.ts:56,72). The tool only trims (tools.ts:1038-1039), and the runner uses the identifier in the unique key and the object key (work-runner.ts:1988,1998). Its description promises 'Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore' but nothing enforces that. REFUTED PART of the failure scenario: a non-DeliverableError does not 'escape the tool'. WorkSession catches every execute() throw and returns 'Tool crashed: <message>' as an error result (runner/agent-core/src/work/session.ts:933-939). Content-Disposition is sanitised (deliverables/index.ts:302-313). What remains: identifiers diverge between the two write paths, local-disk storage throws on '..', and an over-long key produces an opaque S3 error.

READ: the runner's stored validation omits details (work-runner.ts:2044-2052), and the route stores them (route.ts:89-104). Impact is latent. rg finds no current web or native consumer of validation.details, so nothing is broken today beyond losing data a future card would want.

READ: DELIVERABLE_VALIDATOR is still 'juno.work.deliverables.validate.v1' (validate.ts:255). `git log -S` shows it introduced only in f66876db (2026-08-05). f490ff0e (2026-08-08) added packageBudgetProblems, relationship checks, formula, named-range and overflow problems, and 546808a9 (same day) reordered the budget gating. Neither bumped the stamp, although its own comment says tightening must not silently relabel old verdicts.

READ: the auditor's failure-dependent scenario holds. Worse, no failure is needed. The codebase states that App Router preserves ChatView across /chat/A → /chat/B (chat-view.tsx:~2233), so useConversationWork, and the useWorkArtifactList state inside it, survives a conversation switch. On a switch, discovery sets run to null, so enabled is false, but `artifacts` keeps A's list. When B's finished session is discovered (179-186), WorkRunPanel renders TerminalRun at once, and WorkDeliverableStage stages A's document under B's title, with a live Download link to A's artifact and an inline preview that starts fetching A's bytes. This lasts until B's SSE snapshot sets run and the new list fetch lands. If that single fetch fails, A's file stays staged under B for good, since `failed` is ignored by the stage. Raised to medium because the common path shows the wrong conversation's file with no failure at all.

READ: the inline preview is always active (work-site-preview.tsx:384,391,397). useSitePreview downloads the whole zip on every activation (440-460), and the route answers with Cache-Control private, no-store (download/route.ts:147). The spreadsheet preview route buffers, hashes and fully loads the workbook (preview/route.ts:78-110; spreadsheet-preview.ts:129). No visibility or on-demand gate exists. The magnitude in the scenario is inflated. Every production deliverable comes from one model tool call whose whole spec, including base64 site assets and every spreadsheet row, the model must emit inline (tools.ts:1015-1030). A 40 MB site or a 50 MB workbook is therefore not realistically reachable, and real re-downloads are KB to low-MB per conversation open.

Auditor rated this major. READ: the stage appears only in TerminalRun (work-run-panel.tsx:356-358) and returns null for non-previewable kinds (stage:42-43). `empty:hidden` removes the slot, and the 'N more files under Outputs' line points at SessionOutputs, which contains only chat artifacts and images (session-outputs.tsx:98-107,137-147). Correction: the invisible kinds are .docx and .pptx. PDF is not a create_deliverable kind (tools.ts:966-978).

The only trace of a file while a task runs is WorkCurrentAction's passing 'Produce the presentation "X"' line, built from the tool summary (work-timeline.tsx:232-237; tools.ts:1031-1035), which disappears on the next tool. 'Created X' events reach derivePerformedActions only for the terminal digest, and only on incomplete runs (work-run-panel.tsx:343-347).

Auditor rated this major. Same evidence as web-work-deliverables-6. The newest-only discovery is limit 1 (use-conversation-work.ts:179). ChatView mounts a single WorkRunPanel beside research's HistoricalResearchRunPanel list (chat-view.tsx:2262-2267). The limitation is acknowledged in the hook header (63-70). A second task per conversation is reachable because start_task is keyed per user message (task-tool.ts:190-203).

missed.title: Stage ignores a failed or pending artifact list: no error, no retry, no fallback to event-derived rows
missed.evidence: READ: WorkDeliverableStage reads only list.artifacts (stage:33-44). useWorkArtifactList exposes `failed` and `reload` (work-documents.tsx:61-66,105-108), but rg finds no reader of documents.failed or documents.reload in src/components/chat or work/detail. The event-derived fallback (`fromEvents`) and the WorkLoadError retry lived only in the unmounted WorkDocuments (work-documents.tsx:111-135). While the list is null, the stage shows nothing, then pops in with animate-rise-in.
missed.failure_scenario: A user opens a conversation whose task finished with a report. The single /api/work/artifacts request fails, a transient 5xx for example. The panel shows status, words and meter but no deliverable, with no error and no retry. The stream already knows a file was created (artifact_created events), and the user is told nothing.

missed.title: Deliverable title is an <h2> nested inside the task panel's <h3>
missed.evidence: READ: WorkRunPanel titles itself with `<h3 id={titleId}>` (work-run-panel.tsx:124) and uses h4 for 'Plan' (230). The stage it contains renders the artifact title as `<h2 className="… text-heading">` (stage:51). That was right for the retired task page's main column, where the stage was top level, but wrong inside the chat panel.
missed.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user navigating by headings meets the deliverable (h2) as a new top-level section that ends the 'Task' (h3) section, and it lists above the transcript's own structure. The document outline no longer shows the file as part of the task that produced it.
